body:
Upstreaming these changes without the rest is useful for typescript etc to derive types from IDL, the other parts around script elements are less well defined so probably shouldn't be upstreamed to HTML yet.

Though potentially as a follow-up we can export an algorithm from the Trusted Types spec, that we call from HTML so we're not monkey patching prepare the script algorithm within Trusted Types forevermore.

> Did we reach agreement on shadowing all these properties?

It's what is now implemented in all 3 major engines. So I guess yes? I'm not sure if this is something that needs further discussion but I guess the cats already out the bag.

Fwiw it specifically came from a WebKit review on the original design being quite complicated and potentially perf sensitive.

> I think we should add some kind of issue marker about the unresolved issues with the script element if we make it appear more complete.

So with these change I did deliberately call into the trusted types spec to avoid anything "unfinished" within the HTML spec itself, but I'm happy to add an issue marker, I'll have a think on exactly what to put in it (happy to take usggestions if you have any)

@annevk out of interest if I rebase this and move an issue block somewhere to the script section to replicate what is mentioned in the trusted types spec above incompleteness, would you be open to accepting it? Or do you want an alternative approach? It would be good to fix the webref issue. If it's not desirable to upstream I can look into alternative fixes for that.
I think that would be good enough, yeah.
@lukewarlow looks like this needs rebasing again. Please ping me on Chat when it's done and I'll try to get to it quickly.

AI review ``` Summary Faithful upstreaming of Trusted Types' HTMLScriptElement monkeypatch, but the port copies two under-specified bits from the Bikeshed source verbatim and drops one required step, plus the IDL loses several cross-reference links. Roughly 4 blockers, 8 suggestions, 3 nits. Blockers - source:67703 — duplicated phrase. Let urlString be the result of be the result of — delete the second be the result of. - source:67234, 67244–67246 — IDL types and extended attribute are unlinked. TrustedScriptURL, TrustedScript (×3) and [LegacyNullToEmptyString] are bare text. Wattsi can only auto-link IDL types that have a local ; these are external, which is exactly why every other site spells them out. Compare source:35302 ((TrustedHTML or DOMString)), source:125697 ((TrustedHTML or [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString)), and source:13043 ([LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString innerText). Fix: TrustedScriptURL, TrustedScript, [LegacyNullToEmptyString]. - source:67673–67687 — textContent setter drops null handling. The IDL type is (TrustedScript or DOMString)? with no [LegacyNullToEmptyString], so the setter genuinely receives null. get trusted type compliant string is defined over "a TrustedType or DOMString input", and DOM's set text content takes "a string value" — neither accepts null. DOM's own setter says "if the given value is null, act as if it was the empty string instead, and then run set text content with this and the given value", and the text being moved says the same thing ("The textContent setter steps are to, if the given value is null, act as if it was the empty string instead, and then do as described below"). Observable: scriptEl.textContent = null under require-trusted-types-for 'script' currently normalizes to "" before the sink check; as written it feeds null to the default policy. Add the null clause. (innerText and text are fine — [LegacyNullToEmptyString] and plain DOMString respectively handle it at the binding layer.) - source:67695–67699 — src getter uses reflection machinery that is no longer in scope. get the element and get the content attribute are algorithms of a reflected target (source:8574–8575), and the element definitions are written in terms of the reflected content attribute name (source:8594–8602), which only has a value when a reflected IDL attribute is defined to reflect it. This PR removes [ReflectURL] from src, so those two steps have no defined meaning. Trusted Types got away with it because those terms were unlinked plain text there; linking them in HTML makes the gap real. Write it directly, mirroring the iframe srcdoc getter at source:36122–36133:

  • Let attribute be the result of getting an attribute by namespace and local name given null, src's local name, and this.

  • If attribute is null, then return the empty string.

  • Let urlString be the result of encoding-parsing-and-serializing a URL given attribute's value, relative to this's node document.

  • If urlString is not failure, then return urlString.

  • Return attribute's value, converted to a scalar value string.

    • - This also removes the pointless element binding (this is the element). Suggestions - source:5011 — wrong fragment for the new external reference. #update-script-trustedness-algorithm is the Bikeshed-generated section heading id in w3c/trusted-types#607, not the . The dfn id will be #update-script-trustedness. Verified against the sibling entry one line up: the dfn is #get-trusted-type-compliant-string while the heading is #get-trusted-type-compliant-string-algorithm. Also note the reference dangles until #607 lands, so land that first. - source:67634, 67658, 67682 — invocation phrasing. w3c/trusted-types#607 declares "To update script trustedness for HTMLScriptElement |script| given string |value|". Use "given compliantScript", not "with". - source:67690–67727 — src algorithms are in the wrong subsection. They sit inside the
    that belongs to the text/supports domintro block. The natural home is the earlier block at source:67533–67586 alongside crossOrigin/referrerPolicy/fetchPriority/async, which directly follows the src content attribute prose and roughly tracks IDL order. - source:67642–67688 — algorithm order doesn't match the IDL. IDL declares innerText, textContent, text; the prose does text, innerText, textContent. Reorder to match. - Dropped author-facing rationale. Trusted Types §4.1.2 carries an intro paragraph ("…adding the innerText and textContent attributes directly on HTMLScriptElement. The behavior of the attributes remains the same as in their original counterparts, apart from the additional behavior of calling get trusted type compliant string") and a Note ("Using these IDL attributes is the recommended way of dynamically setting the URL or a text of a script. Manipulating attribute nodes or text nodes directly will call a default policy on the final value when the script is prepared"). Neither survives, so a reader hitting source:67244–67245 has no explanation for why two inherited members are redeclared. Carry over at least the note, and/or add an IDL comment. - source:67256–67258 — XXX wording and issue-link format. "The script element processing by Trusted Types is still largely defined in that specification, and has some missing steps that are expected of implementations" is hard to parse. Cross-repo issues are cited qualified elsewhere (w3c/csswg-drafts issue #1088 at source:1745; w3c/IntersectionObserver#464 at source:8364), so bare "issue #507" misleadingly reads as whatwg/html. Suggested:

    Trusted Types processing for the script element is still largely defined in Trusted Types, and does not cover everything implementations are expected to do. See w3c/trusted-types#507. TRUSTED-TYPES

    - ( after matches e.g. source:8395.) - source:67256 — XXX placement. As positioned it splits the element's
    from its opening description ("The script element allows authors to include dynamic script…"), making an editorial marker the first prose a reader sees. Consider moving it next to the new algorithms. - source:67724–67725 — setter phrasing. "Set this's src content attribute to compliantScriptURL" is valid HTML idiom (cf. the async setter at source:67578), but its closest analogue — the TT-derived srcdoc setter at source:36147 — uses "Set an attribute value given this, srcdoc's local name, and compliantString". Matching that would keep the two TT ports symmetric. - Also mention the fix in the commit message. Trusted Types' text setter sets the slot and does String replace all with the given value, not the compliant string; this PR correctly uses compliantScript in both steps. That's a genuine (if obviously intended) behavior change, which sits awkwardly with "This has no behaviour changes and is just moving spec text". Nits - source:3451–3452 — the two new DOM entries are bare
  • while most of that list reads "The … algorithm" / "The concept of …". Optional: fold into one
  • The get text content and set text content algorithms
    • . - source:67244–67246 — an IDL comment marking the three members that shadow Node/HTMLElement would help; the spec already uses inline IDL comments here (// also has obsolete members). - PR hygiene — the checklist is entirely unchecked even though this is already-shipped behavior with existing coverage: wpt has trusted-types/HTMLScriptElement-internal-slot.html, trusted-types/block-text-node-insertion-into-script-element.html, and trusted-types/script-enforcement-*.html. Filling in tests/implementer boxes (or stating "spec move, no new behavior") would settle it. The PR Preview build is red purely from a Wattsi 503, so re-trigger it before landing given the IDL changes. Overall Not mergeable yet — the textContent null branch and the src getter's dependence on reflection internals are substantive, and the missing IDL links plus the duplicated phrase are mechanical must-fixes. All four blockers are localized, so one focused round should clear them. Separately, your first review question is still open: nothing in the PR body records agreement to shadow innerText/textContent on HTMLScriptElement, and that's the one thing a reviewer can't resolve from the diff. Happy to trim this to just the blockers if you'd rather post a short round first. ```

AI feedback ## Summary This is a re-review at e9302ba. The latest commit fixes every finding from the earlier AI review in the thread: the `src` getter rewrite, `textContent` null handling, linked IDL types, algorithm order, the XXX's wording and placement, the restored note, and the IDL comment. Checked against the surrounding spec: - Lint and a full build, including the developer edition, both pass. - Chromium, Gecko and WebKit all ship exactly this IDL. - The `src` setter correctly uses DOM's *set an attribute value*. That algorithm has no Trusted Types (TT) hook, so the default policy doesn't run twice. What's left is coordinating with the TT dependency, w3c/trusted-types#607, and fixing a note that is partly wrong. That comes to 1 blocker, 3 suggestions and 2 nits. ## Blockers - **source:5018** — the `#update-script-trustedness` anchor isn't in the published TT spec yet. It only appears once w3c/trusted-types#607 merges. That PR is already approved, but it has two problems that affect this one: - **The dfn markup.** It reads ``, and Bikeshed ignores the attribute's value (it only checks that `export` is present). That's why the anchor is `#update-script-trustedness` today. If someone fixes it to the evidently intended `export for="HTMLScriptElement"`, Bikeshed generates `#htmlscriptelement-update-script-trustedness` instead. You can see this with *script text*, which is published as `#htmlscriptelement-script-text`. This link would then break silently. - **The step.** Its only step says "Set `[=this=]`'s `[=script text=]` value to `|value|`", but it should say `|script|`. It only works because HTML calls it from setter steps, where `this` is the script. - **Fix:** make it a plain `` in the TT PR (or add `for=` and update `data-x-href` here to match), and use `|script|`. Then land the TT PR before or together with this one. It also removes TT's "Update the `text` setter steps as follows" monkey patch, which would duplicate HTML's new `text` setter if it were left in place. ## Suggestions - **source:67755–67764** — the restored note is wrong in two ways. It was written into TT before DOM had its attribute hooks. - **Attribute nodes.** It says manipulating attribute nodes "will instead invoke the default policy … when the script is prepared". That's false for `src`. All of these call TT's *get trusted type compliant attribute value* when the attribute changes: - `setAttribute()` and `setAttributeNS()` - *set an attribute*, used by `setAttributeNode()` - *set an existing attribute value*, used by `Attr`'s `value`, `nodeValue` and `textContent` That algorithm's table has an `HTMLScriptElement` `src` row, so each of these is checked against the same "HTMLScriptElement src" sink. WPT covers this in `trusted-types/block-string-assignment-to-Element-setAttribute.html` and `block-string-assignment-to-attribute-via-attribute-node.html`. Only text-node changes are deferred until the script is prepared. So the `src` IDL attribute is no more "recommended" than `setAttribute()`. The note also reads oddly right after "Changing any of these attributes dynamically has no direct effect", which includes `src`. - **`innerText`.** The note recommends `innerText`, but *set the inner text steps* turns line breaks into `br` elements. For example, `script.innerText = "// x\nfoo()"` leaves the child text content as `// xfoo()`, which is all comment. Under enforcement, the stored script text then no longer matches, so the default policy runs anyway. This is w3c/trusted-types#517, which is still open. - **Fix:** drop `src` and `innerText` from the recommendation. Consider moving the note after the `script.text` domintro (source:67886); it stays in the dev edition there. For example: ```html

The text and textContent IDL attributes are the recommended way of dynamically setting the text of a script element, as their setters check the given value against Trusted Types. TRUSTED-TYPES Manipulating text nodes directly will instead invoke the default policy on the element's child text content when the script is prepared. (The innerText setter also checks the given value, but replaces line breaks with br elements, which are not part of the child text content.)

``` - **source:67770–67773** — the XXX only points at w3c/trusted-types#507. HTML now owns the `innerText` setter, which stores the given value in step 2 and inserts `br` elements in step 3. That mismatch is exactly what w3c/trusted-types#517 is about, so add a sentence and a link for it. - **PR hygiene** — the checklist is still entirely unchecked, and the PR body doesn't record evidence for the first-round question about agreement on shadowing. It could link: - **Implementers:** all three engines ship this exact IDL, including the shadowed `innerText`/`textContent` and `[LegacyNullToEmptyString]` on the `innerText` string member. See Chromium's `html_script_element.idl`, Gecko's `HTMLScriptElement.webidl` and WebKit's `HTMLScriptElement.idl`. - **Tests:** `trusted-types/block-string-assignment-to-HTMLElement-generic.html` (covers `innerText`/`textContent` on `script`), `block-string-assignment-to-text-and-url-sinks.html` and `HTMLScriptElement-internal-slot.html`. - **Implementation bugs:** not applicable, since this has already shipped. ## Nits - **source:5013** (existing code, outside the diff) — `tt-trustedscript` links to `#trusted-script`, which is TT's section heading. The interface dfn is `#trustedscript`, like the neighbouring `#trustedhtml` and `#trustedscripturl`. This PR adds three more IDL uses, so it's worth fixing in passing. - **Commit message:** - "the changes to HTMLScriptElement's IDL that was previously patched by the trusted types specification" should be "that were previously monkey patched by the Trusted Types specification". - "src and text properties" should say "IDL attributes". - The title says "IDL changes", but the commit also adds getter and setter steps. - "aside from fixing a handful of spec only mistakes" could list them. The `text` setter stored the given value rather than the compliant one, the `src` getter relied on reflection internals, and the `textContent` setter's null handling was carried over too. That's also the kind of pointer requested for the commit message on w3c/trusted-types#607. ## Overall This is close. The HTML algorithms and IDL now look right, and nothing in the diff itself is a correctness problem. It needs one more round to fix the note and add w3c/trusted-types#517 to the XXX. Separately, the TT PR's dfn and step need fixing, and it needs to merge first; after that, this can land.
I've done everything except for the implementors links I'm not sure where would be best to put them or what to really say.

AI feedback Re-review at 432eef9, which addresses everything from the previous AI feedback. w3c/trusted-types#607 now has both fixes too (w3c/trusted-types@6f76766). Lint and a full build (including the developer edition) pass, and the PR still merges cleanly onto current `main`. One XXX block needs moving and rewording, and there's a template for the implementer links below. That's 0 blockers, 1 suggestion and 2 nits. ## Summary What changed: - **`TrustedScript` link:** `tt-trustedscript` now points at `#trustedscript`, which also fixes the existing `TimerHandler` link. - **Note:** it now recommends only `text` and `textContent`, explains the `innerText` line-break problem, and sits after the `script.text` domintro. It appears in the developer edition. - **XXX:** a new one points at w3c/trusted-types#517. - **PR body:** new commit message, and the checklist is filled in. - **w3c/trusted-types#607:** it's now a plain ``, so the anchor stays `#update-script-trustedness` and matches source:5018. Its step now uses `|script|`. ## Blockers None in the diff. The only thing blocking landing is the order: this can't land before w3c/trusted-types#607 merges, because `#update-script-trustedness` doesn't exist in the published TT spec until then. ## Suggestions - **source:67764–67768** — the new XXX about w3c/trusted-types#517 sits at the top of the `src`/`crossOrigin` block, but it's about the `innerText` setter, which comes after the domintro. Move it to just after that setter (after source:67917). The wording also needs two fixes: - **"The given value":** it says the setter stores "the given value", but it stores the compliant string, which a default policy can change. The commit message says this same imprecision was fixed for `text`. - **`br` elements:** it reads as if `br` elements are always inserted, but that only happens when there are line breaks. Suggested text: ```html

The innerText setter stores the compliant string as the script element's Trusted Types script text, but then replaces any line breaks in it with br elements, so the element's child text content no longer matches. See w3c/trusted-types#517.

``` ## Nits - **Commit message** — there's trailing whitespace: two spaces after "respectively." and a long run after the first bullet. It can be stripped when squashing. The title still says "IDL changes", but the first paragraph now mentions the getter and setter steps, so it's fine. ## Overall This is ready apart from the XXX move and rewording, which is small enough to fix at merge time. It can land once w3c/trusted-types#607 has merged.
